<!-- pr-reviewer: 6162e8b14119c9763ee28e743d2d47841815f6b9 -->
**Needs changes before merge: the branch now conflicts with main (merge main, one hunk). The code itself reads sound.**

**Where it ran.** Not built. I started `pr-test.yml` for this head (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43517553977). It stopped at "Trial merge with main": main is now 7d87985 (PR 1561, Slot entity law, merged), and `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` conflicts. A conflict is no pass, and nothing was built or tested locally either. I read the diff, tests and decision file, and checked with `git merge-tree`.

**What looks good**
- Safety direction: the only behaviour change is `Circular` going from `DepthLaw::None` to `authored_law(src)`. That is `Section` for a whole-model `SrcRef::Entity`, and `None` for Stock and picks. It sits after the `!part_solid` early return, so a Stock source, or an entity that is the setup's stock, is unchanged. No case that was refused now posts, and no judged material is narrowed. I read this; I did not run it.
- A whole-model Circular through a wall now carries blocking `Warning::Gouge` on the op itself. Before, only the program-level stock sim held the post.
- New code is `Option`/match only: no unwrap, expect or panic. The tests are in the owning crate (`crates/app/tests/` imports app commands, posting and MCP; the law table is in-crate). `generate.rs` was already far over 400 lines and grows by about 20 (not blocking). The new test files are 40 and 204 lines.
- On "would the new tests fail on the old code": I did not run them. By reading, the unit tests asserting `Section` and the wall and MCP tests fail with the Circular arm at `None`. The author's M1 to M4 mutation table says the same, and I did not re-run it.
- The decision file records the coarse-STL chord-sag cost (a 32-chord hole, 0 left, is refused). That is stricter, never looser.

**Requested before merge**
1. Merge current main into the branch and resolve `generate.rs` (`depth_law_of`, around line 3363 on main). Main added `OpParams::Slot { .. } => DepthLaw::Section` (PR 1561) and no `authored_law`. The PR's doc comment (the "Slot and Circular cut authored geometry..." bullet) and its Circular arm sit in the same region. Keep both: Slot's arm as main has it, plus `OpParams::Circular { .. } => authored_law(src)`. Update the doc comment to match. Then re-run the Circular suite (`circular_entity_law`, `authored_law_tests`) and the touched Slot tests.
2. PR 1563 (OpFrame) needs no change: `depth_law_of` is still called once in `generate.rs` (line 2850 on main), and `OpFrame::material_of` wraps `judged_material` only. The Circular law is independent of it. Confirm after the merge that the wall test still convicts.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The body and decision say `authored_law` is shared with the Slot (#1537). Main's Slot arm is `Section` for picked and whole-model sources alike, so after the merge `authored_law` has one caller. Say so in the decision, or have the Slot arm call it. Your choice.
- A mechanical remerge of main is allowed under "refresh only at merge time" when this PR is next in a batch.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6162e8b14119c9763ee28e743d2d47841815f6b9 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The fix itself is sound. The branch now conflicts with main (#1561 merged at 22:22 UTC during this review), and the merged #1561 makes the `authored_law` docs untrue.

### What looks good
- The root cause is right. Before this PR, `depth_law_of` gave every Circular `DepthLaw::None`. The fix routes Circular through `authored_law(src)` after the `part_solid` early return. Entity becomes `Section`. Stock, and an entity that is the setup's stock, stay unjudged.
- The tilted/offset path is covered by reading the code. The `Some(frame)` branch feeds `model: (depth_law == DepthLaw::Section).then_some(&m_gen.facets[..])` (generate.rs, frame verify), so a tilted setup is judged in its own frame. No test exercises it.
- Every probe I ran showed judging without moving the tool. The path-equality pin (`a_whole_model_circle_inside_the_modeled_hole_stays_clean`) proves it for the legal circle.
- My own probes (local scratch tests, not pushed) gave these results:
  - A whole-model circle cut 2 mm below a **blind** floor: 2053 `Gouge` warnings.
  - A whole-model circle at the floor: clean.
  - A whole-model circle in the stock *beside* the part (centre outside the part outline): clean, so there is no false refusal off the part.
  - The same Entity job with a rotated stock, where the program sim refuses to judge: 2053 gouges and the post is blocked. The op's own verdict now holds the post where the sim can't.
- The provenance line, the Gate map line and the decision file are present. No goldens, snapshots or process files change.

### Results merged with main (locally)
The tests ran on the PR head trial-merged with upstream main **f402b368**, which was main before #1522 and #1561 merged. Against the current main (7d879850) the merge conflicts, see 1 below.

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| circular_entity_law | 4 passed |
| camcraft-app `--lib` (incl. `authored_law_tests`) | 208 passed |
| circular_pick | 4 passed |
| circle_centre | 5 passed |
| operations | 119 passed, 6 ignored |
| verify | 21 passed, 2 ignored |
| mcp_verify | 3 passed |
| mcp | 22 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| solid_law_goldens | 7 passed |
| golden_cl | 32 passed |
| mill2d_b / units_in_refusals / slot_caps | 9 / 5 / 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutations** (each reverted after):

| mutation | integration suite | law table |
|---|---|---|
| M1: Entity -> `None` | wall + MCP tests fail | 2 fail |
| M2: Selection -> `Section` | **survives** | 2 fail |
| M3: Circular arm hoisted above the `part_solid` early return | **survives** | `a_source_that_is_not_the_part_is_never_judged` fails |
| M4: Entity -> `Contain` | **survives** (all 4) | 2 fail |
| M5: Stock -> `Section`, early return kept | survives (unreachable, as designed) | 1 fails |

**Chord sag**, measured on a radius-10 hole with a 6 mm end mill and a whole-model source. The number is the gouge count:

| chords (sagitta) | leave 0 | leave 0.01 | leave 0.02 | leave 0.05 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 (0.048) | 1026 | 1024 | 768 | 0 |
| 48 (0.021) | 960 | 384 | 0 | 0 |
| 64 (0.012) | 512 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 96 (0.005) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 128 (0.003) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

A circle is refused exactly when sagitta > leave + ~0.01 (`GOUGE_TOL`). That is sane: the mesh says the material is there. It does go further than the decision file says, because a 64-chord hole is refused at leave 0, not only a 32-chord one. Worth one line in the decision file.

### Requested before merge
1. **Merge conflict with main** in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, in the `depth_law_of` doc comment, after #1561 (`OpParams::Slot { .. } => DepthLaw::Section`). The code arms do not overlap. Keep main's Slot bullet and rewrite the Circular bullet so it points at `authored_law`.
2. **The `authored_law` docs are now untrue.** The new doc comment on `authored_law` (generate.rs, "the Slot's endpoints and width, #1537"), the test comment "The one law #1537's Slot shares" (`crates/app/src/operation/authored_law_tests.rs:36`) and the decision file all say the Slot uses this helper. #1561 merged without it: the Slot takes `Section` for **every** part-solid source, picks included, so the Slot and `authored_law` disagree on `Selection`. Either:
   - re-scope the comments to Circular only, or
   - better, see note A: make `Selection -> Section` and have the Slot arm call `authored_law` too, so the "one shared law" is real.

### Questions / notes (not blocking unless you take note A into this PR)
- **A. #1550 is a gouge that can post, not only a missing warning.** A picked Circular (floor face at Z 4, bottom typed at Z 1, so 3 mm into the floor) with a **rotated stock** makes the program sim refuse to judge ("the program sim models an axis-aligned stock"). `uncovered()` in `posting_sim.rs` then accepts the fresh op's own verdict, and with law `None` that verdict has no gouge. In my run the post was blocked only by an unrelated `RapidInStock` on the ring-change retract (move 2069). A path without that rapid would post the 3 mm overcut. The same applies to every other case where the sim refuses (posed or tilted moves, rotary, lathe frames).
  - With M2 applied (Selection -> `Section`), circular_pick, mill2d_b, units_in_refusals, golden_cl and solid_law_goldens all still pass, and the same job then carries 2053 gouges.
  - That is the law the Slot's picks take on main since #1504.
  - Suggest raising #1550 from P3 to P1 and fixing it here or right after.
- **B. M4 (`Contain`) survives the integration suite.** It also matched `Section` on every probe above (chord-sag table identical, beside-part clean). `rims_of` declares nothing for Circular, so the rim-excusal concern in the decision file is hypothetical today. The choice is pinned only by the table, which is fine as long as the decision file says so.
- **C. M3 (placement) survives the integration suite.** Only the table's `SrcRef::Entity("stock")` case pins the early-return order. An integration pin with an Entity source naming the setup's stock entity would make the placement behavioural. Optional.
- The PR body's "Not stacked: #1537's branch did not exist..." paragraph is stale now that #1561 has merged.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 42c36dd1c32af423f3fc405df7ba63303eead0c3 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Built and tested on the merged tree; one stale-comment note below, not blocking.

**What looks good**
- The merge since 6162e8b1 is one commit (42c36dd1c). Its `git show --remerge-diff` shows the one hand-resolved hunk, the doc comment above `depth_law_of` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, and nothing else. The result keeps both bullets: Circular via `authored_law`, and Slot as `Section` for a finished-part source (#1504, #1537). In the head, the Slot arm (`OpParams::Slot { .. } => DepthLaw::Section`) and the Circular arm (`OpParams::Circular { .. } => authored_law(src)`) are both present, in that order, with the same meaning as on main and on the earlier head.
- Gouge verdict direction, case by case. The only code change to a law is the Circular arm, `None` to `authored_law(src)`, and it sits after the `!part_solid` early return:
  - Stock source, or an entity that is the setup's stock (`part_solid` false): `None` before, `None` now. Same.
  - Picked source: `None` before, `None` now. Same.
  - Whole-model `SrcRef::Entity` on a finished part: `None` before, `Section` now. Stricter (the op now carries blocking gouges for a circle through a wall); `Section` only adds checks, it narrows no judged material.
  - No case gets looser, so no blocker. Read from the code and confirmed by the tests, not by a mutation run of mine.
- No other kind's law changes: the diff to `depth_law_of` touches only the Circular arm and doc text. Contour/Face, picked pockets, Drill/Bore/Thread, Slot all unchanged.
- No unwrap/expect/panic added outside tests. Tests are in the owning crate (`crates/app/tests/circular_entity_law.rs`, 204 lines; in-crate `authored_law_tests.rs`, 40 lines). `generate.rs` was already far over 400 lines and grows by ~20 (not blocking). No golden, snapshot, process-file or dependency changes. No hold in the PR body, comments or reviews.

**Results merged with main, on the self-hosted runner** (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43519808123, main 1dce70b5):
| step | result |
|---|---|
| quick gate, app suites (175 by gate map, incl. `circular_entity_law`, `circular_pick`, `slot_picks`, `slot_caps`, `slot_pick_refusals`, `mill2d_b`, `units_in_refusals`, `solid_law_goldens`, `posting`, `mcp`, lib incl. `authored_law_tests`) | ok, 669 s, 0 failed |
| quick gate, ui suites | ok, 53 s, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

No `cfg(windows)` or per-OS values in the diff, so no local Windows re-run was owed.

**Do the new tests fail on the old code?** Not re-run by me on this head. The previous review (6162e8b1) ran the author's mutations M1 to M5 locally: with the Circular arm back at `None`, the wall test, the MCP test and the table tests fail. The code in the arms is unchanged since, so that result stands.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The earlier request (review of 6162e8b1, item 2) about stale `authored_law` docs is only half done: the `depth_law_of` bullet is fixed, but the `authored_law` doc comment ("the Slot's endpoints and width, #1537", generate.rs), the test comment "The one law #1537's Slot shares" (`authored_law_tests.rs:36`) and `docs/decisions/1543-circular-entity-law.md` lines 8-9 still say the Slot uses this helper. It does not: the Slot arm is `Section` for picks as well, and `authored_law` has one caller. Comment-only; re-scope them to Circular whenever convenient. I am not holding the merge for it.
2. The earlier notes A (#1550, a picked Circular below its floor with a stock the program sim cannot judge may post) and the chord-sag table (a 64-chord hole is refused at leave 0, not only a 32-chord one) stand as follow-ups; they concern behaviour this PR does not change.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
